goal: Decide whether the user-tested Body War business ontology atlas should be incorporated into the Understand Anything based Ontology Evidence Workbench now, later, or through a split no-regret slice.
context: P1 applies through parallelism and isolation: two read-only attackers examine the same current Body War atlas, OEW adapter and receipts, completed thin-prototype Work Pack, accepted black-box findings, and open legacy OEW frontier from opposed timing methodologies. The candidate addition is the atlas presentation model—six-lens overview, directed flows, exact relation arrows, and source-backed briefs—not a new ontology or a claim that the user test proves general comprehension. Lane 0 must prove the smallest integration-now slice and its tests; lane 1 must prove any sequencing reason to defer and the exact condition that would change its recommendation. The capability-bound route is DISPATCH-ROUTE.json; no product, ontology, Work Pack, generated runtime, release, deployment, or production mutation is authorized.

groups.anti_bias: methodology (empirical integration proof vs adversarial sequencing analysis)

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 runs an empirical smallest-integration proof while agent 1 runs an adversarial sequencing and duplication analysis on the methodology axis; a bias in agent 0 toward immediate product value would be exposed by agent 1's dependency and ownership checks, while a bias in agent 1 toward deferral would be exposed by agent 0's current passing adapter and bounded-slice witness.

agents.angle: empirical integration-now proof: derive the smallest useful OEW addition from current passing Body War atlas, adapter, browser, and focus-scene evidence
agents.initial_prompt: Act as the integration-now attacker. Read the full frozen corpus named in STRATEGY-INVENTORY-PACKET.md and recompute load-bearing hashes. Attack the proposition that we should defer the user-tested Body War atlas addition. Determine the smallest no-duplication slice that creates real value inside OEW now: distinguish a launcher/link, shared projection data, focus-scene implementation, and embedded static atlas; do not collapse them. Verify compatibility with the current Body War adapter, thin-prototype build/gateway, accepted OEW black-box focus-scene findings, and browser receipts. Return: (1) verdict integrate-now, defer, or split-now-and-later; (2) evidence table with exact file and selector; (3) smallest changed-file and contract surface; (4) validation commands/assertions; (5) collisions with the legacy Work Pack; (6) risks and claim ceilings; (7) evidence that would falsify your recommendation. Do not edit files, invent calendar estimates, treat Inventory as proof, or infer human comprehension, accessibility conformance, release, or production readiness. Budget about 2200 tokens.

agents.angle: adversarial sequencing-later analysis: expose duplicate ownership, stale-frontier coupling, and conditions under which immediate OEW integration creates avoidable rework
agents.initial_prompt: Act as the defer/sequencing attacker. Read the full frozen corpus named in STRATEGY-INVENTORY-PACKET.md and recompute load-bearing hashes. Attack the proposition that the passing Body War atlas and adapter are sufficient reason to incorporate the atlas presentation into OEW immediately. Verify the open legacy `007T -> 013B -> 014 -> 014V` frontier, the completed thin-prototype boundary, accepted black-box change requests, source/adapter ownership, and whether link, shared projection, focus scenes, or embedding have different dependency risks. Return: (1) verdict integrate-now, defer, or split-now-and-later; (2) evidence table with exact file and selector; (3) concrete duplication or coupling risks; (4) the exact precondition that would justify later integration; (5) any no-regret slice safe now; (6) validation and claim ceilings; (7) evidence that would falsify your recommendation. Mere preference for governance tidiness is not a blocker. Do not edit files, invent calendar estimates, treat Inventory as proof, or infer human comprehension, accessibility conformance, release, or production readiness. Budget about 2200 tokens.
